title: Spurious Aft Hold Smoke Warnings in Heavy Rain — Norvik Cargo Lines
abstract: Norvik Cargo Lines reports smoke warnings in the aft hold during and shortly after heavy rain loading, with nothing found on inspection, forcing three diversions in eighteen months and a loss of confidence in a warning the crew must act on.

sections.request: We load in the open at northern stations and in bad weather we get a smoke warning in the aft hold, usually in the climb, sometimes on the ground before the doors are shut. The crew has to treat it as real, so we have discharged the bottles twice and diverted three times in a year and a half, and every time the hold was clean. Our loaders think it is the wet air coming off the cargo when the hold warms up. Whatever it is, the crew cannot tell a real fire from this, and that is the part we cannot live with. We need the warning to mean something.
sections.background: The first two events were investigated as detector faults and the detectors were changed with no improvement. A third event on a different airframe pointed us at the pattern rather than the parts. Our reliability team correlated eleven events against station weather and found every one of them within four hours of loading in rain or wet snow. We have since changed our loading procedure to sheet the pallets, which halved the rate but did not stop it.
sections.expected_outcome: A detection arrangement that does not raise a warning on humid air alone, with the same or better response to a genuine fire. We would accept a longer confirmation time if it is certified and written into the crew procedure, because a false warning that leads to a discharge is worse for us than a few seconds of delay.

type_data.business_justification: Three diversions and two extinguisher discharges in eighteen months, each with a full hold inspection and a bottle replacement, and an erosion of crew confidence in a warning that has to be actioned without question.
